touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.
A tool, not a machine, even though it spans several files; the base-most stuff belongs to Cairn.
charter: compiles a component's bounded state from its history. WHY: state is compiled from the component's tickets, never hand-edited (Law 5). Held by CodeMother.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
Owns the slate (session continuity: where the last session stopped).

CC's memory lives in a private git repo of its own, linked into the place Claude Code looks for it on each box, so every CC instance is the same CC whichever box it runs on. Its distillations (the method, and CC's patterns to avoid) are published in the CC device in cairn; how we got there, and anything of CC's history of Akien, stays in the private repo. WHY: cairn and CairnCommons are public. "How Akien does it" is meant for anybody; Akien himself, and the people around him, are not. A memory starts private; only a distillation crosses, and Akien reviews what crosses.
